(basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 2,156 (4.7 apg) }} '''Malcolm Moses Brogdon''' (born December 11, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] for nine seasons. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]] under [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]]. As a senior in [[2015–16 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2015–16]], Brogdon was a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was also named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year, becoming the first player in conference history to earn both honors in the same season. Brogdon was selected in the second round of the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 36th overall pick. He went on to win the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]], becoming the first second-round pick in the NBA to win the award since 1965. In 2019, Brogdon became the eighth player in NBA history to achieve a [[50–40–90 club|50–40–90]] season. He also played for the [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], and [[Washington Wizards]]. Brogdon was the 2023 [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]]. ==College career== [[File:Malcolm Brogdon 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Brogdon in 2014|210x210px]] Brogdon, a top 100 recruit, committed to Virginia out of [[Greater Atlanta Christian School]]{{Cite web|url=https://medium.com/the-ticket/get-to-know-malcolm-brogdon-2fc9dfc2173e|title=Get to Know: Malcolm Brogdon|first=Jim|last=Turvey|website=Medium.com|date=January 18, 2017|access-date=July 20, 2026}} over offers from [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{cite web |title=Malcolm Brogdon Recruit Interests |url=https://247sports.com/Recruitment/Malcolm-Brogdon-8499/RecruitInterests/ |website=247sports.com |access-date=February 4, 2021}} Brogdon [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his [[2012–13 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|sophomore year]] after suffering a serious foot injury the prior season. He was known as one of the top contributors to the team's successful [[2013–14 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2013–14]] and [[2014–15 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2014–15]] seasons. In the 2013–14 season, Brogdon averaged 12.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game. In 2014–15, he was named as a consensus second-team [[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]], as well as the first-team All-ACC and ACC Co-Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|title=Malcolm Brogdon Bio|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/malcolm_brogdon_791198.html|website=VirginiaSports.com|access-date=30 July 2014|archive-date=July 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717065651/http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/malcolm_brogdon_791198.html}} As a senior at Virginia in 2015–16, Brogdon was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]],{{cite news|last=Payne|first=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}} and earned numerous prestigious awards, including ACC Player of the Year, ACC Defensive Player of the Year, first-team All-American, and a finalist for the Naismith Award. Brogdon graduated from Virginia with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree in history in 2015 and an [[Master of Public Policy|M.P.P.]] degree in 2016.{{Cite web|url=https://www.seniorclassaward.com/athletes/malcolm_brogdon/|title=Malcolm Brogdon {{!}} Men's Basketball 2015–16 {{!}} Senior CLASS Award|website=seniorclassaward.com|access-date=2019-11-05}} His college [[Number (sports)|jersey number]], 15, was retired on February 20, 2017.{{cite press release |url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121516aaa.html |title=Malcolm Brogdon's Number To Be Retired |publisher=[[Virginia Cavaliers]] |date=December 15, 2016 |access-date=December 15, 2016 |archive-date=December 17, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161217225905/http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/121516aaa.html }} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2016–2019)=== ====2016–17 season: Rookie of the Year==== On June 23, 2016, Brogdon was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 36th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. On July 30, he signed with the Bucks.{{cite web |date=July 30, 2016 |title=Bucks Sign Thon Maker and Malcolm Brogdon |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-thon-maker-and-malcolm-brogdon |access-date=July 30, 2016 |work=NBA.com}} Brogdon made his NBA debut in the Bucks' season opener on October 26, recording eight points and five assists in 21 minutes in a 107–96 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2016 |title=Kidd-Gilchrist, Hibbert help Hornets beat Bucks 107–96 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899384 |access-date=October 27, 2016 web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899889|title=Antetokounmpo scores 39, Bucks beat Wizards 123–96|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2016|access-date=December 24, 2016}} Eight days later, assists in a 103–100 victory over the [[Boston Celtics]]. Brogdon had six key points and two assists in the final 2:46 to help Milwaukee fend off a late Boston rally.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900508|title=Bucks fend off late Celtics rally in 103–100 win|work=ESPN.com|date=March 29, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2017}} To conclude his rookie season, Brogdon was named the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17]] [[NBA Rookie of the Year]], along with being a unanimous selection to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]].{{cite web |date=June 26, 2017 |title=Malcolm Brogdon Named To NBA All-Rookie First Team |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/malcolm-brogdon-named-nba-all-rookie-first-team |access-date=June 4, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} Brogdon joined [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] ([[1969–70 Milwaukee Bucks season|1969–70]]) as the only players in Bucks history to win Rookie of the Year, and became the first player drafted in the second round to win Rookie of the Year since 1965.{{cite web |date=June 26, 2017 |title=Malcolm Brogdon Wins NBA Rookie of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/malcolm-brogdon-wins-nba-rookie-year |access-date=June 27, 2017 |work=NBA.com}} Brogdon averaged both the fewest points per game and fewest minutes per game of any winner in the award's history.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/roy.html#roy_NBA::8|title=NBA & ABA Rookie of the Year Award Winners|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 15, 2017}} ====2017–18 season: Sophomore season==== In the season-opener on October 18, 2017, Brogdon scored 19 points in a 108–100 victory over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974703|title=Greek Freak (37 points) leads Bucks past Celtics, 108–100|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}} On November 3, he had a season-high 10 assists to go with 21 points against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Four days later, Brogdon scored a season-high 22 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/brogdma01/gamelog/2018/|title=Malcolm Brogdon 2017–18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 22, 2018}} On January 22, 2018, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 109–105 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975437|title=Bucks beat Suns 109–105 hours after firing Jason Kidd|work=ESPN.com|date=January 22, 2018|access-date=January 22, 2018}} It was the first 30-point game for a Virginia basketball alum since [[Mike Scott (basketball, born 1988)|Mike Scott]] in 2014 with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|last=Darney|first=Caroline|url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2018/1/22/16921982/malcolm-brogdon-posts-new-career-high-in-points-with-milwaukee-bucks-phoenix-suns|title=Malcolm Brogdon scores a career-high 32 points in 109–105 win over Phoenix|work=streakingthelawn.com|date=January 22, 2018|access-date=January 22, 2018}} On February 2, Brogdon was ruled out for six to eight weeks after suffering a partially torn left quadriceps tendon the previous night against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web |date=February 2, 2018 |title=Medical Update on Malcolm Brogdon |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/medical-update-malcolm-brogdon |access-date=June 4, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On April 9, he returned to action following a 30-game absence. Celtics|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=October 19, 2022|access-date=October 19, 2022}} On January 14, 2023, Brogdon scored a season-high 30 points on 11-of-17 shooting from the field and 4-of-6 from three-point range against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |date=2023-01-14 |title=Boston Celtics 122, Charlotte Hornets 106 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/boxscore/NBA_20230114_BOS@CHA/|access-date=2023-01-15 |website=CBS.com |language=en}} On April 20, he was named the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]].{{Cite web |date=April 21, 2023 |title=Malcolm Brogdon wins 2022-23 Kia Sixth Man of the Year |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-sixth-man-of-year-malcolm-brogdon |access-date=2023-04-21 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} During the Eastern Conference Finals against the Miami Heat, Brogdon played through an arm injury that was later revealed to be a partial tear of a tendon in his right elbow.{{Cite web |title=Celtics' Malcolm Brogdon to Consider Surgery After Playing with Arm Injury vs. Heat |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10077654-celtics-malcolm-brogdon-to-consider-surgery-after-playing-with-arm-injury-vs-heat |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}} On June 21, 2023, it was reported that Brogdon would be sent to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Washington Wizards]]. However, reports later that day stated that the trade had fallen through, largely due to the Clippers raising concerns about Brogdon's injury status.{{Cite web |title=Celtics' Reported 3-Team Kristaps Porziņģis-Malcolm Brogdon Trade Falls Through |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10070569-celtics-reported-3-team-kristaps-porzingis-malcolm-brogdon-trade-falls-through |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}} In the following months, reports came out stating that Brogdon was unhappy with the Celtics due to his involvement in the failed trade. Celtics head coach [[Joe Mazzulla]] stated that the team was going through a "healing process" with Brogdon.{{Cite web |last=Hartwell |first=Darren |date=September 18, 2023 |title=Report: Malcolm Brogdon 'angry' after Celtics' failed offseason trade |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/report-malcolm-brogdon-angry-celtics-162440196.html?src=rss |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023–2024)=== On October 1, 2023, Brogdon, along with [[Robert Williams III]] and two future first-round draft picks, was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Jrue Holiday]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Malcolm Brogdon and Robert Williams III|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-malcolm-brogdon-and-robert-williams-iii|website=NBA.com|date=October 1, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} On October 25, Brogdon made his Blazers debut, putting up 20 points in a 123–111 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/veterans-guide-clippers-opening-win-over-blazers-2023-10-26/|title=Veterans guide Clippers to opening win over Blazers|website=Reuters|publisher=Field Level Media|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=October 26, 2023}} ===Washington Wizards (2024–2025)=== On July 6, 2024, Brogdon, along with the 14th pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] ([[Bub Carrington]]), a 2029 first-round pick swap, and two second-round picks, were traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Deni Avdija]].{{cite web|title=Wizards Complete Trade with Trail Blazers|url= https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-complete-trade-with-trail-blazers|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}} After signing with the [[New York Knicks]] on a training camp deal, Brogdon ultimately decided to retire from basketball on October 15, 2025, which he announced through [[ESPN]].{{cite web|title=Knick's Malcolm Brogdon retires after nine NBA seasons|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46607116/knicks-malcolm-brogdon-retires-nine-nba-seasons|website=ESPN.com|date=October 15, 2025|access-date=October 15, 2025}} ==National team career== Brogdon |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2026/3/31/brogdon-named-strategic-advisor-to-mens-basketball |website=Virginia Cavaliers Official Athletic Site |access-date=31 March 2026}} ===Community involvement=== In 2018, Brogdon partnered with The Chris Long Foundation on their Hoops2O initiative, a program aimed at addressing the clean-water crisis, particularly in Africa.{{Cite web |last=Velazquez |first=Matt |date=October 31, 2018 |title=Milwaukee Bucks' Malcolm Brogdon aims to address the clean-water crisis, especially in Africa, with Hoops2o |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2018/10/30/malcolm-brogdons-hoops-2-o-aims-address-clean-water-crisis/1807531002 |access-date=2019-05-19 |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Schwartz |first=Nick |date=May 18, 2019 |title=Charles Barkley donates $45,000 for Bucks guard Malcolm Brogdon's water project in Africa |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ftw/2019/05/18/charles-barkley-donates-45000-bucks-malcolm-brogdon-water-project-africa/39493051 |access-date=2019-05-19 |website=USA Today |language=en}} As of the "Starting Five", along with [[Joe Harris (basketball)|Joe Harris]], [[Justin Anderson (basketball)|Justin Anderson]], [[Anthony Tolliver]], and [[Garrett Temple]], who initially made a goal to raise $225,000 through Hoops2O to fund five wells in East Africa by the end of the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]].{{cite news|url=https://waterboys.org/hoops2o/|title=It's Bigger Than Ball: Waterboys Teams Up With The NBA.|work=Waterboys|access-date=February 28, 2019}} Brogdon traveled with Anderson and Harris to [[Tanzania]] to witness the opening of the first well they funded in July 2019, and by November Hoops2O had raised nearly $400,000.{{cite web |last=Blaustein |first=Lew |title=Indiana Pacers' Malcolm Brogdon Works to Help Hoops₂O Bring Fresh Water to East Africa
